questions.question_text: Consider two events, event A and event B, occurring within the same process where event A happens before event B. If event A has a Lamport logical clock timestamp C(A) = 12, what is the minimum possible integer timestamp C(B) for event B, given that clock updates follow the rule C(e) = monotonically increasing integer?
questions.explanation: Because Lamport logical clocks assign monotonically increasing integer timestamps and event A happened before event B within the same process, C(B) must be strictly greater than C(A). Thus, 12 + 1 = 13.
questions.learning_objective: Define core terminology associated with distributed systems

source_citation.quote: Lamport Logical Clocks assign a monotonically increasing integer timestamp C(e) to every event. If event a happens before b within the same process, C(a) < C(b).

questions.verifier_notes: Lamport clocks assign monotonically increasing timestamps. If event A happens before event B in the same process, C(A) < C(B). Given C(A) = 12, the minimum next integer timestamp for C(B) is 12 + 1 = 13.
